questions.question: Which of the following identity is correct regarding GNP?

options.text: GNP = GDP + Factor income earned by the domestic factors of production employed in the rest of the world + Factor income earned by the factors of production of the rest of the world employed in the domestic economy

GNP = GDP - Factor income earned by the domestic factors of production employed in the rest of the world - Factor income earned by the factors of production of the rest of the world employed in the domestic economy

GNP = GDP - Factor income earned by the domestic factors of production employed in the rest of the world + Factor income earned by the factors of production of the rest of the world employed in the domestic economy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GNP = GDP + Factor income earned by the domestic factors of production employed in the rest of the world - Factor income earned by the factors of production of the rest of the world employed in the domestic economy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The** gross national product (GNP**) is an estimation of the** total worth of all finished goods and services** produced over a** specific time period** using resources owned by th**e citizens of a nation**.
 
• Commonly, the gross national product is determined by** adding up** all **domestic private investment, domestic government spending, net exports, and any resident income** from overseas investments, then **deducting foreign resident income.**
 
• The difference between a **country's exports and any imports** of goods and services is what is known as **net exports.**
 
• A superset of the** GDP** is the GNP.
 
• While** GDP limits its examination of the economy** to the nation's borders, GNP expands it to include the** net foreign economic activities** carried out by its citizens.
 
• GNP and GDP can have** different values**, and a significant gap between them can indicate a** country's level of economic integration.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **total monetary worth** of all completed goods and services produced in a nation d**uring a given time period **is known as the **gross domestic product (GDP).**
 
• An **estimate of a nation's GDP** can be used to determine the **size and growth rate **of an economy.
 
• **Spending, output, and income** can all be used to compute GDP, which can then be adjusted for **population and inflation **to give more detailed results.
 
• **Real GDP** takes into account the **effects of inflation** while **nominal GDP** does not.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct regarding 'Monsoon'?

options.text: The word monsoon is derived from the Arabic word and it refers to the seasonal reversal in the wind direction during a year.
The word monsoon is derived from the Tamil word and it refers to the seasonal reversal in the wind direction during a year.
The word monsoon is derived from the Tamil word and it refers to the seasonal reversal in the wind direction every month.
The word monsoon is derived from the Arabic word and it refers to the seasonal reversal in the wind direction every month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The word monsoon is derived from the Arabic word and it refers to the seasonal reversal in the wind direction during a year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Monsoon**

 
• Monsoons are basically seasonal winds that reverse their direction according to the change in season.
 
 
• They are periodic winds.
 
 
 
• They travel from the sea to the land in the summers and from land to the sea during the winters.
 
• India gets southwest monsoon winds in the summers and northeast monsoons during the winters.
 
• The Southwest monsoon arises because of the formation of an intense low-pressure system over the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• The Northeast monsoon arises due to the high-pressure cells formed over the Siberian and Tibetan plateaus.

The reasons responsible for the monsoon winds in India are the following:

 
• Intense heating of the Tibetan plateau during summer months,
 
• Vast land area,
 
• Permanent high-pressure cell in the South Indian Ocean (east to northeast of Madagascar in summer),
 
• Subtropical Jet Stream (STJ),
 
• Tropical Easterly Jet (African Easterly Jet),
 
• Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone,
 
• Strengths of Low pressure over Tibet and high pressure over the southern Indian Ocean,
 
• Somali Jet,
 
• Somali Current,
 
• Indian Ocean branch of Walker Cell,
 
• Indian Ocean Dipole.

questions.question: Which of the following is a diverse group of aquatic organisms capable of photosynthesising?

__
 
• Algae

 
 
• Algae are a diverse group of aquatic organisms that have the ability to conduct photosynthesis.
 
• Algae are prominent in bodies of water, common in terrestrial environments, and are found in unusual environments, such as on snow and ice.
 
• Algae grow on wood in wet, dark conditions.
 
• The study of algae is known as **phycology**.
 
• Most of the soil algae, especially blue-green algae act as cementing agents in binding soil particles and thereby preventing soil erosion.
 
• In uncropped soil, soil algae check the loss of nitrates through leaching and drainage.
 
 
 
• **Algae can be classified on the basis of the pigments present in them**.
 
 
• Chlorophyceae – green algae
 
• Phaeophyceae – brown algae
 
• Rhodophyceae – red algae
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Yeast belongs to the kingdom of fungi. It is a eukaryotic unicellular fungus that is used in bread making. 
 
• Saccharomyces cerevisiae is commonly known as baker's yeast.
 
• Baker's yeast comes in a variety of forms, including active dry, fresh (or cake), liquid, and instant.
 
• Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a type of budding yeast that can ferment sugar into carbon dioxide and alcohol, is widely used in the bread-making and brewing industries.
 
 
 
• ​Protozoa​
 
 
• Protozoa mainly feed on bacteria, but they also eat other protozoa, and sometimes** fungi**.
 
• Some protozoa absorb food through their **cell tissues**.
 
• All protozoa digest their food in stomach-like **compartments**.
 
• As they digest, they make and give off nitrogen, which is an element that plants and other higher creatures can use.
 
 
 
• **Fungi​**
 
 
• Fungi constitute a unique kingdom of heterotrophic organisms.
 
• Fungi show a great diversity in morphology and habitat.
 
• Fungi are cosmopolitan and occur in air, water, soil, and animals and plants.
 
• The study of fungi is Mycology.

questions.question: Carbon dating means __________.

options.text: a method to determine the density of fissile material
a method of calculating the remains of sulphur and nitrogen in hard rock
a method of calculating the age of very old objects by measuring the amounts of different forms of carbon in them
a method of determination of weight of a very old rock

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__a method of calculating the age of very old objects by measuring the amounts of different forms of carbon in them__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carbon dating:

 
 
• Carbon dating is a technique used to determine the approximate age of once-living materials.
 
• It is also referred to as Radiocarbon dating.
 
• Radiocarbon dating is a method of estimating the age of an artefact or biological vestige based on the relative amount of various isotopes of carbon present in a sample.
 
• Age can be estimated by measuring the amount of carbon-14 present in the sample and comparing this against an internationally used reference standard.
 
• Radiocarbon decays slowly in a living organism but once the organism dies, it ceases to absorb Carbon-14 so that the amount of the radiocarbon in the tissues steadily decreases.
 
• Because carbon-14 decays at a constant rate, an estimate of the date at which an organism dies can be made by measuring the amount of its residual radiocarbon.
 
• It was developed in the late 1940s by Williard Libby.
 
• Carbon dating is one of the most effective tools in the archaeologist's kit.
 
• It is a vital part of the investigation and preservation of our past.
 
• The oldest dates that can be reliably measured by this process date to approximately 50,000 years.
 
• Histories of archaeology often refer to its impact as the "radiocarbon revolution".
 
• Radiocarbon dating has allowed key transitions in prehistory to be dated, such as the end of the last Ice Age, and the beginning of the Neolithic and Bronze Age in different regions.
 
 

Thus, we can say that Carbon dating is **a method of calculating the age of very old objects by measuring the amounts of different forms of carbon in them.**__

questions.question: The ratio between the nominal and real GDP is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GDP deflator**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In economics, the GDP deflator (implicit price deflator) is a measure of the level of prices of all-new, domestically produced, final goods and services in an economy.
 
• The formula implies that dividing the nominal GDP by the Real GDP will give the GDP deflator, hence "deflating" the nominal GDP into a real measure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National income:**

 
 
• **​**National income is the total value of a country’s final output of all goods and services produced in a year.

 
 
• National income is also known as NNP at factor cost.
 
• It is sum total of incomes of residents of a country in a given period of time including capital consumption or depreciation.
 
• All payments that are made to factors of production like land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship are at the factor cost at which goods and services are produced.
 
 
• National income = NNP at factor cost__
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Gross value added**:**
 
 
• **GVA of a sector** is defined as** the value of output minus the value of its intermediary inputs**. This “value added” is shared among the primary factors of production, **labour and capital**.
 
• GVA= GDP + subsidies on products – taxes on products.
 
 
• As the total aggregates of taxes on products and subsidies on products are only available at whole economy level, Gross value added is worked for computing gross regional domestic product and other measures of the output of entities smaller than an entire economy.
 
 
 
• It can also be worked to compute how much money a product or service has contributed toward meeting a company's fixed costs.
 
 
 
• Green GDP - is defined as data obtained after the deduction of the cost of resources, environment, and human health from the traditional GDP.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of river lengths?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ganga: **

 
 
• **​**The length of the river Ganga is 2,525km.
 
• Ganga is a transboundary river of South Asia. It flows through India and Bangladesh.
 
• The river originates from the Gangotri glacier which is situated in the western Himalayas in Uttarakhand.
 
• The river flows south and east through the Gangetic plain of India and Bangladesh and finally emptied into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The left-bank tributaries are Gomti, Gandak, Ghaghra, Kosi, Ramganga and Mahananda and the right-bank tributaries include Yamuna, Son and Damodar, Tamsa and Punpun rivers.
 
 
 
• **Godavari:**
 
 
• **​**The Godavari river is the largest river system in Peninsular India.
 
• Godavari river rises from Trimbakeshwar near Nasik in Maharashtra and flows for a length of about **1465 km** before outfalling into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Tributaries: Pravara, Purna, Manjra, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Pranhita (combined flow of Wainganga, Penganga, Wardha), Indravati, Maner and the Sabri.
 
 
 
• **Krishna:**
 
 
• **The length of the Krishna River is 1400 km** and the coverage area is 258,948 square km.
 
• Krishna River is the fourth largest river in India after Ganga, Godavari, and Brahmaputra.
 
• It traces its course through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh states of India.
 
• The tributaries of the Krishna River are Bhima, Tungabhadra, Veena, Panchganga, etc.
 
• The Krishna river finally falls into the Bay of Bengal at Hamsaladeevi in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The area of the drainage basin of the Krishna River is 258948 square km.
 
• Bhima, Dindi, Peddavagu, Musi, etc are the left bank tributaries of the Krishna River.
 
• Kudali, Venna, Koyna, Panchganga, etc are the right bank tributaries of the Krishna River.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna:**
 
 
• River Yamuna originates from Yamunotri Glacier in Uttarakhand Himalayan Region.
 
• **The length of River Yamuna is around 1376 Km** and it merges with River Ganga at Prayagraj (Allahabad) Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The river Yamuna is the longest tributary of the river Ganga.
 
• River Yamuna flows through Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Delhi.
 
• Some of the important cities in the bank of river Yamuna are Agra, Mathura, Delhi, Prayagraj (Allahabad).

questions.question: The moon completes ____ rotation on its axis as it completes one revolution around the Earth.

• Thus, the rotation time of the** moon to rotate on its axis overlaps with its revolution along with the orbital plane**. The **moon completes 1 rotation on its axis as it completes one revolution around the Earth**. As a result, we will see somewhat, **Moon always has the same face towards the earth**.
 
• The moon travels around the earth in an elliptical orbit.
 
• When the moon is closest to earth, its rotation is slower. so an additional **8 degrees** are visible on the **eastern side**.
 
• When the moon is farthest from the earth, its rotation is faster. so, an additional 8 degrees are visible on the **western side**.

• Full moon: On this day, a perfect round-shaped moon appears.
 
• Crescent Moon: The shape of the moon during the phases between the new moon and half-moon is the crescent moon.
